source.title: Size Scaling in Self-Play Reinforcement Learning

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling analysis to AlphaZero self-play reinforcement learning on three board games, using Elo and PolyRank ratings rather than language-model held-out loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-size scaling of game ratings, not held-out cross-entropy loss, language-model extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its results are recorded as evidence about scaling in the tested RL setting; they do not directly establish loss scaling. Four separately trained instances were used for each NN size; the paper reports group averages and ranges rather than individual-instance results.
record.test_reason: The study trains AlphaZero self-play agents of varying network width on three games and fits rating against parameter count. This bears on whether a scaling law of the same form appears in an RL regime (V5). Elo is linear in log(params), which is equivalent to Bradley-Terry strength µ = n^γ. That is a power law in parameters, but on game strength, not held-out loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one fix: PolyRank shows slight flattening for larger models in all three games, 'especially' Connect Four, not only Connect Four. The authors conclude Elo scales logarithmically with NN size across games and depths. This yields an outcome law depending only on the size ratio, and they suggest universal scaling laws may exist in RL and adversarial games.
record.recipe_differences: Uses AlphaZero self-play RL on board games and measures Elo/PolyRank game ratings against parameter count; it does not measure language-model held-out loss, dataset size, or training compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted Elo scaling exponent γ differs by game and Connect Four depth. PolyRank shows slight flattening at larger sizes for Connect Four.

fits_no_version.finding: Game win probability depends only on the ratio of network sizes between opponents, P_A = 1/(1+(n_B/n_A)^γ), with a game-specific γ between 0.352 and 0.648.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In self-play RL on zero-sum games, relative playing strength follows a power law in parameter count with a game-dependent exponent.

record.peer_reviewed: The European Symposium on Artificial Neural Networks proceedings, 2022
record.problems: The study measures game ratings rather than held-out loss; it covers only three games and a limited set of depths. Each NN size has four trained instances, and the uncertainty ranges are shown graphically without numeric bounds in the text.

untested.parts: Loss-based power laws: the measure is Elo/PolyRank, not held-out loss. Scaling with data or compute is untested, since training steps are fixed. Other modalities (image, video), repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are untested. Parameter range and orders of magnitude are not stated in the text.
Not tested: no extrapolation to larger runs.
Not tested. Depth (2 vs 3 layers) is varied only for Connect Four, and with different training steps; no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Not tested for language models. γ differs by game (0.352–0.648), but that concerns a different construct.

missing.what: Range of parameter counts or widths tested, and how many orders of magnitude are spanned; not given in the text, figures only
Authors' statement that the log trend will break for large models without hyperparameter adjustment, or as optimal play is approached

record.verdict_notes: Borderline relevance. The construct is game strength rather than loss; it is kept under V5 as an RL training-regime scaling law of power-law form via the Bradley-Terry strength. Only model size is varied. Training steps differ for the Connect Four 3-layer runs (4×10^3 vs 2×10^3). Four instances per size; no numeric uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute in language models.
Prediction of much larger runs' held-out loss from fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.

relationships.condition: Elo ratings of AlphaZero MLP agents trained by self-play on Connect Four (2 and 3 layers), Oware and Pentago, with training steps fixed so the largest models converge
relationships.reason: Elo is log-linear in parameter count in all four settings, i.e. strength is a power law in parameters (r1–r4). PolyRank also shows a log-scale trend (r6, r7). The measure is game rating, not loss.
relationships.display_finding: Elo increased log-linearly with parameter count in all four settings, implying power-law strength scaling, while PolyRank also showed a logarithmic trend.

relationships.condition: Bias-free PolyRank ratings, particularly Connect Four with 2 hidden layers
relationships.reason: PolyRank shows slight flattening for larger models, especially in Connect Four (r5). The authors also say the trend will break near optimal play or without hyperparameter retuning.
relationships.display_finding: PolyRank ratings flattened slightly for larger models, especially in Connect Four; the authors also expected the trend to break near optimal play or without hyperparameter retuning.
